name: Pickaxe
style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Kenney Survival Kit)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: Plan row 204 (Quaternius static Pickaxe via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is tool-pickaxe.glb from Kenney's CC0 Survival Kit (zip pinned by sha256; the kit page links the current zip). The kit has two pickaxes: tool-pickaxe (wooden haft, steel collar and a double-pointed steel head, 74 tris) and tool-pickaxe-upgraded (steel haft with a short wood grip wrap and steel pommel, 110 tris); both were rendered and the plain one was taken because the wooden haft under a steel head is the classic pickaxe read, while the upgraded one is almost all steel and reads more like a hammer. The Kenney colour map is flattened to 12 colours: the two oranges are the haft (wood: amber over sky) and the ten greys/blue-greys the head and collar (steel: moon over sky, threshold 0.2), the same pairs as the axe and sword. Height 0.85 m, butt to the top of the head (a 36-inch pick is about 0.9 m); the head is stylized wide, 0.63 m tip to tip and 0.14 m deep. Kept faceted (smooth: false). Rest pose: upright, haft along +Y with its butt on y = 0 and its axis on x = z = 0 (the head is symmetric, so the centred bbox leaves the haft on the origin); bare tapered haft 0 to 0.57 m, steel collar 0.57 to 0.64 m, head block 0.71 to 0.85 m with the picks at 0.74 to 0.82 m. The picks are turned 35 degrees about +Y (ingest.yaw 35) so the hero view shows them broadside; rotate the model by -35 degrees about Y to lay them along X. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand and offset by (0, -0.12, 0) m in the pickaxe's frame for the lower hand near the butt (a second hand goes at about y 0.40 m for a two-handed swing), then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and a pick faces the swing. Static, no clips.
